text:
Predicates:
Visited(x, y) ::: x visited y.
MountainRange(y) ::: y is a mountain range.
LocatedIn(y, z) ::: y is located in z.
Mine(y) ::: y is a mine.
Donated(y) ::: y has been donated.
HasMine(y) ::: y has a mine.
In(z, w) ::: z is in w.
Premises:
Picuris(y) ∧ MountainRange(y) ∧ LocatedIn(y, NewMexico ∨ Texas) ::: The Picuris Mountains are a mountain range in New Mexico or Texas.
Visited(JuanDeOnate, y) ::: Juan de Onate visited the Picuris Mountains.
HasMine(y) ∧ Donated(y) ::: The Harding Pegmatite Mine was donated.
¬∃x (MountainRange(x) ∧ LocatedIn(x, Texas) ∧ HasMine(x) ∧ Donated(x)) ::: There are no mountain ranges in Texas that have mines which have been donated.
Conclusion:
Visited(JuanDeOnate, y) ∧ LocatedIn(y, Texas) ::: Juan de Onate visited a mountain range in Texas.
